edges.rationale: Slow start's exponential cwnd growth and its termination by ssthresh or a loss event presuppose the definitions of the congestion window and the loss signals introduced in this leaf.
AIMD's linear cwnd increase and multiplicative decrease on loss cannot be understood without first knowing what cwnd is and how loss (triple duplicate ACKs vs. timeout) is detected.
Congestion avoidance begins when cwnd reaches the slow-start threshold (ssthresh) defined during slow start; the phase transition is a direct dependency.
Fast retransmit is triggered by three duplicate ACKs, which is one of the loss-signal distinctions (triple duplicate ACK vs. timeout) established in this leaf.
Fast recovery implements the multiplicative-decrease step (halving cwnd on a triple duplicate-ACK loss) whose role in the AIMD cycle is defined in the congestion avoidance leaf.
The Tahoe-vs-Reno contrast (timeout-driven reset to slow start vs. fast recovery) only makes sense once slow start behavior is understood.
The fairness convergence argument is a direct analysis of the additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease dynamics, so AIMD must be learned first.
